synopsis: PEGASUS was a German on-road research project for validating one Level 3 highway automation function; it ran from 1 January 2016 to 30 June 2019 (42 months), with 17 partners, about 1,791 person-months (149 person-years), and approximately EUR 34.5 million including EUR 16.3 million in public subsidy [f15693, f15694, f15695]. Its output was a validation method rather than a certified product or approval, combining a scenario database from field recordings with simulation, proving-ground testing and field tests [f1290, f1546, f1778]. Its functional, logical and concrete scenario levels subsequently entered ISO 34501–34505 and underpin the booklet's scenario catalog [f6735, f13258]. The booklet uses PEGASUS and related programs as schedule-forecasting precedents: capability building took years, and follow-on VVM added another four-year cycle, July 2019–June 2023, with EUR 47 million volume [f15713, f15717, f1205, f1549]. These are on-road reference cases for planning first-of-a-kind virtual safety testing, not a measured duration for validation after capability becomes available [f9614, f1776]. Evidence quality remains a material caveat: the accounts rely on consortium self-reporting despite being labeled independent, and later chapters say PEGASUS and VVM were not individually verified and should be checked before review [f1294, f7701, f11276].
